record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: Let X be a Banach space with the alternative Daugavet property and assume X contains no copy of ℓ_1. Determine whether X must then satisfy n(X) = 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Let X be a Banach space which does not contain any copy of ℓ1 and having the alternative Daugavet property. Is it true that n(X) = 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a (real or complex) Banach space with unit ball $B_X$ and unit sphere $S_X$. For a bounded linear operator $T \in L(X)$, the numerical radius is defined by
$$v(T) = \sup\{|x^*(Tx)| : x \in S_X,\ x^* \in S_{X^*},\ x^*(x) = 1\},$$
and the numerical index of $X$ is
$$n(X) = \inf\{v(T) : T \in L(X),\ \|T\| = 1\}.$$
The space $X$ is said to have the alternative Daugavet property if
$$\max_{|\omega|=1} \|\mathrm{Id} + \omega T\| = 1 + \|T\|$$
holds for every rank-one operator $T \in L(X)$ (equivalently, for every weakly compact operator $T \in L(X)$).

Assume that $X$ has the alternative Daugavet property and that $X$ contains no isomorphic copy of $\ell_1$. Must $X$ satisfy $n(X) = 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal extensive follow-up work on the alternative Daugavet property, numerical index 1, lushness, and slicely countably determined (SCD) spaces, but no source clearly settles the specific question of whether a Banach space with the alternative Daugavet property and no copy of $\ell_1$ must have numerical index 1. Partial results exist in special classes (e.g., spaces with 1-unconditional basis and rearrangement invariant spaces, where the equivalence of ADP and $n(X)=1$ is known), but a general resolution was not located.

status_evidence.title: Lushness, numerical index 1 and the Daugavet property in rearrangement invariant spaces
status_evidence.snippet: For spaces with 1-unconditional bases, lushness, the alternative Daugavet property and numerical index 1 are equivalent; in r.i. sequence spaces only c0, ℓ1 and ℓ∞ have these properties.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results equate ADP with n(X)=1 in restricted classes, but the general question remains unresolved in the located literature.

status_evidence.title: The alternative Daugavet property and examples
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ADP and connections to numerical index 1.
status_evidence.claim: No general theorem found stating ADP plus no copy of ℓ1 implies n(X)=1.
